A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete 22-page documents, including Appendices A–G. Text and rendered pages support reliable comparison; pages 2–22 are identical.

before.justification: v2 reports original sufficiency-probing, QA, efficiency and ablation results, plus synthetic-label experiments and a TREC in-context-learning case study in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original empirical results in Sections 3–4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same attention-head probes, classifier ensemble, incremental context processing with KV caching, and self-prompting alternative. No algorithm or model component changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six QA datasets with short and extended contexts, and retain the TREC in-context-learning scenario in Appendix E. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Full Context, BM25, SBERT, LLMLingua, LongLLMLingua, LLMLingua2, FT and Self-Prompt. Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and appendix experiments.

E3.justification: The reported splits, sample sizes, model configurations, default 10% chunking, compression settings and evaluation metrics are identical, including the settings documented in Appendices A, C and F.

E4.justification: The threshold, chunking, latency, head-selection, ensemble-size and synthetic-label analyses are retained unchanged. Appendix E's model-specific cutoff case study and Appendix G's high-precision recall analyses also match.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including the cross-validation description. v3 adds no run or seed disclosures, uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 2 retains 39.2 overall accuracy for Ours, and Table 8 retains synthetic-label overall F1 scores of 84.6 and 87.0 for the 1B and 8B models.

T1.justification: Section 2's chunk and prefix definitions, sufficiency-threshold formulation, and ensemble and cache equations are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical claims about latent sufficiency signals, dynamic cutoff, efficiency and accuracy, and larger-model self-assessment. The new title does not alter these contributions.

C2.justification: The interpretations of scaling, stopping tradeoffs and model-specific sufficiency are unchanged. Sections 4.5–4.6 retain the same applicability qualifications and limitations for holistic and open-ended tasks.

D1.justification: The labeling procedures, prompts, hyperparameters, training details and hardware information in Appendices A, D and F are identical. The code-access statement is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 37 references are unchanged, including positioning relative to context compression, RAG and research on knowledge encoded in model activations.

P1.justification: The title changes from Language Models (Mostly) Know When to Stop Reading to Knowing When to Stop: Efficient Context Processing via Latent Sufficiency Signals. The arXiv version/date stamp also changes; all other text and document structure remain identical.

P2.justification: All 11 figures and 11 tables retain their formatting, captions and placement. Rendered pages 2–22 are pixel-identical; the first page retains its layout, differing only in title and version/date text.

improvement.justification: v3 retitles the paper and updates its version stamp while preserving the scientific argument, empirical evidence, limitations, reproducibility information and presentation throughout the appendices. These editorial changes do not establish a meaningful overall quality improvement or decline.
